newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Nov 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Nov 18.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President Ramos belittled the capability of leftist groups to disrupt the APEC Summit meetings in Manila and at the Subic Freeport. Three big leftist groups plan to stage parallel fora and protests this week.(INQUIRER,CHRONICLE,PHILIPPINE STAR,TIMES JOURNAL)

- President Ramos said its all systems go for the APEC which starts Wednesday saying there is no need to overwork the security because it is in place and that APEC leaders, their delegations, as well as media and other businessmen are assured of their safety. (MALAYA,BULLETIN)

- APEC director-general of the national organising committee Lisandro Abadia accused organisers of anti-APEC fora of receiving millions of pesos from unknown foreign sources to sabotage the APEC summit questioning how they could afford to have the Manila Midtown Ramada Hotel booked exclusively for their foreign delegates. (STANDARD)

- The 600-strong pilots' union at the Philippine Airlines yesterday said they may have to go on strike anytime after negotiations for a new collective barganining agreement (CBA) got bogged down on Friday night. (MANILA TIMES)

- The Office of the President is worried about the Congress delaying approval of the excise tax reforms on beer and cigarettes saying this will have an adverse impact on government's revenues for 1997. (BUSINESSWORLD)

- The Philippines has joined an international group, the Asia Pacific Market Surveillance Group, formed to stop market manipulation and illegal dealings in the stock exchanges in the region. The Philippines has been named as one of its founding members. (INQUIRER)

- The Board of Investments (BOI) will ask hundreds of firms enjoying fiscal incentives to sell at least 10 percent of their shares to the public as part of a renewed drive to enforce an old BOI policy that has remained unimplemented. (TIMES)

- The country's local exchange operators have raised serious concerns on bidding rules proposed by the National Telecommunications Commission (NTC) for allocating new frequency bands for public mobile telephone services. Globe Telecom and Smart Communications said the bidding rules effectively singled out new local exchange carriers and penalized them beyond what the law provides. (BULLETIN)

- The government has no plans of fully privatising state and controlled corporations involved in key industries such as utilities, steel and banking, Finance Minister Roberto de ocampo said. (TIMES JOURNAL)
